A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiDi-Instruct research. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-generation experiments, component ablations, model-scaling results, zero-shot evaluations, and protein-generation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds downstream evaluations, diversity measurements, practical speed benchmarks, and sampler sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The IKL objective, discriminator-based rewards, grouped normalization, score decomposition, model architectures, and two-phase RGAS algorithm remain. Remark 3.3 adds stabilization details without establishing a newly introduced component; the changed guidance ramp is an experimental parameter revision.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU domain adaptation and GLUE MRPC paraphrase classification, substantially extending evaluation beyond generation and likelihood. PubMed also gains a fine-tuning evaluation, whereas v1 used it for zero-shot likelihood. Existing OpenWebText, seven-corpus zero-shot, and protein-generation coverage remains.

E2.justification: The core benchmark comparators remain. The latency comparison changes from GPT-2, teacher, AS, and RGAS in v1 Figure 3 to AR, MDLM, SDTT, and DiDi-Instruct in v3 Table 7. Appendix A.3 additionally reports a preliminary adapted-DiMO text experiment with entropy 4.0; v1 discussed DiMO without reporting this comparison.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a separate 1,024-sample MAUVE/Self-BLEU evaluation, downstream fine-tuning and classification protocols, protein clustering metrics, and a latency benchmark using H100, bfloat16, and batch size 16. The reported early-stage RGAS guidance ramp changes from 0–30 in v1 Appendix F.3 to 30–40 in v3 Appendix E.5. This documents a setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds RGAS parameter landscapes and global sensitivity analysis, text fidelity/diversity analysis, and protein clustering to investigate mode collapse. These examine robustness and diversity beyond v1's component ablations and structural-confidence measurements. The original cumulative and leave-one-out studies remain, while the AS–RGAS quality–latency curve is removed.

E5.justification: v3 adds fANOVA variance estimation using 1,000 sampled hyperparameter pairs at each of three NFE budgets. Appendix D.1 newly acknowledges variation across baseline training runs and explains reporting published scores matching the strongest reproductions. These disclosures do not provide run counts, seeds, or repeated-run uncertainty intervals for the headline comparisons.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results in Tables 6–7 and 9–13, including 2366.604 tokens/sec at 16 NFEs, PubMed post-adaptation perplexity 24.894, and MRPC accuracy/F1 of 62.3%/73.3%. These are newly reported evaluations, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings. Tables 1–2, the seven-corpus zero-shot values, and the scaling and pLDDT results remain; the earlier latency curve and many text excerpts are omitted or replaced.

T1.justification: The reward definition accompanying Theorem 4.1 in v1, renumbered Theorem 3.1 in v3, changes from log pν minus log pθ to log qν minus log qθ. This corrects the statement to use forward marginals, consistent with the IKL objective and existing appendix derivation. The principal assumptions, proofs, and density-ratio lemma otherwise retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies v1's categorical claim of outperforming the teacher and GPT-2 with 64× acceleration to comparable or superior performance with up to 64× acceleration. The central distribution-matching novelty, few-step generation contribution, and headline OpenWebText results remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of adversarial optimization stability, an exploration–exploitation mechanism, and difficulties transferring DiMO from image tokens to text. It interprets the new sensitivity results as guidance for tuning h versus M and explicitly discusses reduced protein diversity at large NFE budgets. These extend the earlier regularization and scaling-limit discussions.

D1.justification: v3 adds baseline reproduction and score-provenance details, stabilization practices, and implementation settings for the new evaluations. Teacher training is documented as approximately 200,000/350,000 steps instead of 5/7 epochs, without establishing whether the underlying runs changed. The front matter replaces the release promise with Code and Project Page links. Conversely, the software-version table and teacher pretraining GPU-hour estimates are removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the new evaluations and newer diffusion-language work, including MAUVE, fANOVA, MMseqs2, Dream, Mercury, Block Diffusion, and Fast-dLLM, while removing Luo's 2023 distillation survey. It expands comparisons with DiMO and trajectory-matching methods, but retains the central positioning relative to Diff-Instruct, SDTT, and DUO. Publication-metadata updates are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and background receive extensive rewriting. Related work is consolidated into Appendix A, the experimental narrative gains a downstream-task section, and the separate language showcase is removed while the long example appendix is heavily condensed. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template, redraws the pipeline in Figure 2, replaces the latency plot with a new comparison table, and introduces sensitivity heatmaps and several result tables. It removes the software-version table, rearranges retained protein illustrations, and substantially changes the text-example displays. Retained plots and tables are also resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support for preserved diversity, downstream utility, and practical efficiency. MAUVE/Self-BLEU, protein clustering, downstream tasks, and specified latency and sensitivity experiments address important gaps in v1's reliance on perplexity, token entropy, and pLDDT. These gains outweigh the loss of software versions and the AS–RGAS latency curve. Limitations remain: Table 6 contradicts the claim of highest MAUVE at every budget, and the nominally frozen MRPC evaluation unfreezes the final encoder block.
